Subject: Amaya discovery follow-up — data retention/deletion SLAs and next steps

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and appreciate the transparency on Amaya's use cases. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can move toward a mutual action plan: 

- Recap: Amaya will use Redwood Hosted API for primary inference and logging; evaluating Dedicated for production (privacy/regulatory) in Q1.
- Security/compliance items we discussed: SOC 2 status, GDPR/HIPAA requirements, deletion SLAs for PII, log retention (application + access logs), and backups.
- Next steps we requested on the call:
  1) High-level SOC 2 status (Type I/II / expected completion date)
  2) Typical retention windows for application data, logs, and backups and whether deletion SLA for customer data is contractually available (e.g., 30d vs 14d)
  3) Kick off the vendor security questionnaire so our InfoSec can evaluate controls — I can send our questionnaire if helpful or you can share yours.

For context, our baseline for Hosted customers is: primary customer data deletion within 30 days after request, logs retained 180 days, backups retained 90 days — but enterprise customers sometimes require tighter deletion SLAs and different log-retention rules. If you can share Amaya's target SLAs we can flag any gaps earlier.

I’ve attached our Vendor Security Questionnaire template to speed review. Could you confirm who on your side should receive the questionnaire and where we should expect the SOC/Security artifact(s)?

Proposed next step: once we have the SOC status + retention targets, we’ll coordinate a short follow-up call with our Security and Legal (Rishi) to talk SLA language and any BAA needs.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the questionnaire template — very helpful. Quick answers below: 

- SOC 2: We are in the middle of our SOC 2 Type II readiness effort. Controls assessment and remediation are complete; we expect the formal Type II report to be issued in Q1 2027 (target: end of March). We can provide a SOC 2 readiness summary immediately and will share the full report as soon as it's available.

- GDPR/HIPAA: Amaya is a HIPAA-covered entity for certain products. We do not currently have a completed SOC 2 Type II, but we have a set of HIPAA controls in place and are open to executing a BAA where required.

- Retention / deletion SLAs (current standard practice):
  • Primary customer data: deletion requests executed within 30 calendar days.
  • Application & access logs: retained 180 days by default.
  • Backups: retained 90 days (rolling).

We can be flexible on deletion SLAs for enterprise contracts — we've done 14-day deletion commitments for a small number of customers with some additional controls and acceptance of a higher support/ops charge.

I’ve uploaded two items for your team: a short SOC2_Readiness_Summary.pdf and our completed Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (filled). Link: https://drive.amayahealth.com/redwood/AMY-4521 

Happy to schedule a 30-min call this week with Rishi/Neha to walk through the questionnaire and any redlines.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Product Security
Amaya Health

Hi Marissa / Neha / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I confirmed with our ops team and added a couple clarifications:

- Deletion SLA: baseline 30 days; we can commit to 14-day deletion for core PII fields under a commercial agreement and a short onboarding checklist (we'd want documented acceptance testing on deletion flows).
- Logs vs PII: application/access logs will remain 180 days. For customers demanding shorter log retention, we can support custom retention policies but that typically requires Dedicated or a contractual change.
- Backups: standard 90-day rolling backups; backups may contain snapshots of data and are subject to our normal restore processes. Deleting from backups can take longer than primary store deletion; we typically document "deleted from primary within SLA, removal from backups on a best-effort basis and documented schedule" — we can add stronger guarantees for Dedicated/Private deployments.

I uploaded the completed Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx and SOC2_Readiness_Summary.pdf to the link below: 
https://drive.amayahealth.com/redwood/AMY-4521

Regards,
Samir
